title: The Bone Market
text: Stalls of yellow bone under lanterns made from skulls, their candles burning in the eye sockets. The merchants have no faces, and still you can tell they are smiling. Every price here is fair, they say. Most of the prices are written in the buyer.

options.label: Pay in kind; the merchant picks whose.

outcomes.text: The merchant takes its due with a little silver knife and gives good weight for it.
They take the coin with a sigh, as if you had refused a gift, and wrap your purchase in cloth that smells of the grave.

options.label: Only look, and keep your hands to yourselves.

outcomes.text: You look. They let you. One stall sells only the sound of your own names, and you hear them all the way out.
You look, and learn how the faceless haggle: never speak first. It is a lesson that stays with you.
